claims.claim: solutions-portfolio.md declares SOL initiatives to be standing commitments with no end date, funded 'the same way engagement work is: out of reimbursements recovered against agreements that each name a period of performance.' But agreements.md's governing 7600A instrument fixes an estimated amount and agreement period that no cumulative 7600B may exceed — the funding mechanism itself is structurally finite. 'No end date' therefore isn't an actual property of these services; it's an unbroken chain of re-signed finite agreements, and projects-in-distress.md names the exact failure mode when that chain breaks ('an IAA expiring before a new one could be signed') as a project-pause trigger. Reversing this bet — giving an initiative a real end date, or a genuinely perpetual funding vehicle — isn't a unilateral TTS call; it requires renegotiating the agreement structure with OGC and every client agency whose 7600A/7600B funds that initiative.

RFC 003 proposes a Senior Cybersecurity Advisor whose hours go to cross-program coordination, advice, hiring support, and training — explicitly 'not work assigned to a single engagement' — and sits in the Front Office rather than on a delivery team. finance-and-billing.md describes TTS's entire revenue mechanism as cost recovery through billable engagement hours, with overhead from TTS/GSA 'allocated and not under our control.' A role structurally unable to bill an engagement has no seat in the only funding model TTS actually runs on. RFC 003 itself concedes the funding source is undetermined at approval time; locking in the position before that's resolved means undoing it later — cutting the role or forcing it into a billable structure it wasn't designed for — depends on whoever controls TTS/GSA overhead allocation, a lever finance-and-billing.md says TTS doesn't hold.

time-tracking-and-rates.md states that when the Tock team enters hours on an absent employee's behalf, 'the timesheet has no field for who submitted the entry' — an entry made by the Tock team and one made by the employee become the same record. finance-and-billing.md treats Tock data as the basis for utilization rate, the organization's primary financial-health metric, and its only accuracy check is supervisors 'double checking' reported hours, not verifying who reported them. Because submitter provenance was never part of the schema, adding it later to support any audit of billing accuracy is a Tock data-model change TTS doesn't unilaterally control, and every record entered before that change stays permanently unattributable.

chat-user-management.md's offboarding conversion disables an account's 2FA and repoints its email to an address 'the organization no longer administers,' so the account's password-recovery path now runs through a mailbox outside TTS control — a state that can only be reversed with the departed person's cooperation. security-incidents.md's confidentiality model assumes that when a credential is exposed, TTS can 'revoke or change the credentials immediately.' For a converted account, that assumption no longer holds: TTS has already handed the recovery boundary to a party it can't act through, so if the external mailbox is later compromised, the standard incident-response remediation (rotate the credential) isn't available for this account, even though the account still retains its DM history and workspace membership.
